To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crystal structure of Mtb ASADH in complex with SMCS has been solved and that it structurally mimics an intermediate state in the reaction mechanism of ASAD H.
the structure of ASDH from M. tuberculosis in complex with glycol and sulfate has been determined and that this complex structure is similar to the complex structure with SMCS and sulfate.
the structures of Mtb-Asd in complex with glycol and sulfate and with SMCS and sulfate have been determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure-function analysis of ASADH and provides the structural basis for understanding its mechanism of action and for designing new antibacterial drug molecules.
the structure and function of a potential drug target enzyme, ASADH, from the human pathogen Mtb.
the identification and structural elucidation of novel targets for drug design against human pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structures of Mtb-Asd in complex with glycol and SMCS reported in this work provide a structural framework for the development of species specific drug molecules against human pathogenic bacteria.
the structure of MtbASADH in complex with SMCS and glycerol has been determined and reported for the first time.
the structures of Mtb-Asd in the glycerol and SMCS complex provide a structural framework for understanding the catalytic mechanism and inhibition of the enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we determined two structures of Mtb- ASADH in complex with ligands, and these structures may help in the design of species-specific inhibitors for this enzyme.
we have reported the first structure of ASADHH37Rv and the structures of the complexes of Mtb-Asd with glycerol (Mtb-Asd-Gly) and S-methyl-L- cysteine sulfoxides (Mtb- Asd-SMCS).
we have determined the crystal structures of two ternary complexes of ASADH and we propose the possible catalytic mechanism of ASAD
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mtb-Asd is a potential target for the discovery of new anti-tubercular drugs.
the Mtb- ASADH-SM CS complex structure is an excellent starting point for structure-guided drug design against Mtb-ASD.
the structures of ASADH in complex with glycolytic intermediates and with SMCS provide new insights into the structure and mechanism of ASADHS.
